column1: # The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2): the base dump and update v131072 (1.1.1). Nintendo SDK 22.2.8, NVN2.

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

column1: # v0 is the base dump the profile was brought up on; v131072 (1.1.1) is the update a NUP carries alone, the whole game. Their modules are the same builds, and the shader tables
# split from v131072 are v0's key for key: the tables are v131072's, so a NUP of the update packs from the profile as it is
# The NPDM declares 48 MiB of system resources. Startup requests a 6.20 GiB heap.
# agl wraps its depth clears in render conditions, as on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders: in Kokiri Forest the main opaque pass tests EQUAL against a copy of the prepass depth
# that a conditional clear (skipped on the console) wiped first, so no lit geometry landed and the full-screen sky showed through everywhere (a white scene)
# The scene camera for MetalFX's motion vectors (DM_UPSCALER=metalfx-temporal, DM_MFX_INTERP; nvn_mfx.inc): gsys's Context uniform block at vertex uniform 0 of the scene passes, the view
# (3x4 rows) at +0x0 and the view-projection at +0x30, as on Donkey Kong Bananza. Read in a run (DM_MFX_PROBE, v131072): the opening's 3D cutscenes and Link's house give a GL perspective
# camera (50 degrees, 16:9, near 0.1, far 25037, no projection offset) in the 1920x1080 D32F depth pass that matches the upscaler's input; 15,000 upscaler frames, none without a camera
# Metal encoding on its own thread: in Link's house at rate 3.0 it takes MetalFX's temporal scaler from 30.7 to 25.4 ms a frame (GPU p50 24.2 to 17.9), and the game's own upscaler stays at 18.7
# The resolution chain the host logs at launch (loader.c res_chain_log) and the launcher's render sizes (settings.py rate_base): the upscaler's output docked (the 2560x1440 window: ResolutionParam's
# FinalImageResolution, one resample), the same with single upscale (the game has no stub for it), handheld 1920x1080, the game's own rates (its palette's scales 0.75 to 0.333: 1.3333 to 3.0),
# and the rate a stage starts at (level 0: 1.3333; in a run docked 1920x1080 -> 2560x1440 from the stage's first frame)
